llm.prompt: How can I track my football stats as a grassroots player?
llm.answer:
You can track your football stats pretty effectively with a mix of **simple manual logging**, **match video**, and, if you want, **wearable GPS/app tools**.

## 1. Decide what stats matter for your position

Don’t try to track everything at first. Pick 5–10 useful metrics.

### For all players
- Minutes played
- Goals
- Assists
- Shots / shots on target
- Passes completed vs attempted
- Tackles won
- Interceptions
- Fouls committed / won
- Yellow/red cards
- Match rating out of 10

### For attackers
- Chances created
- Successful dribbles
- Crosses
- Pressures leading to turnover
- Offsides
- Expected goals “rough estimate” if you want to get advanced

### For midfielders
- Forward passes
- Key passes
- Ball recoveries
- Duels won
- Turnovers/lost possession
- Successful switches of play

### For defenders
- Clearances
- Blocks
- Aerial duels won
- 1v1s won/lost
- Defensive errors
- Successful long passes

### For goalkeepers
- Saves
- Goals conceded
- Claims/catches
- Punches
- Distribution accuracy
- 1v1 saves
- Clean sheets

---

## 2. Use a simple match log

After every game, record your stats while the match is still fresh.

You can use:

- Notes app
- Google Sheets / Excel
- Notion
- A printed notebook
- A football-specific app

Example table:

| Date | Opponent | Position | Minutes | Goals | Assists | Shots | Pass % | Tackles | Rating | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 03/10/26 | FC United | CM | 80 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 78% | 5 | 7.5 | Good pressing, tired late |

Also add a short reflection:

- **What went well?**
- **What needs improving?**
- **One focus for next match**

This turns your stats into actual development.

---

## 3. Track “easy live stats” during the game

Some stats are hard to remember afterward. Ask a teammate, coach, parent, or friend to record basic events during the match.

Use simple tally marks for:

- Shots
- Goals
- Assists
- Tackles won
- Key passes
- Lost possessions
- Saves
- Fouls
- Interceptions

They don’t need to be perfect. Consistency matters more than precision at grassroots level.

---

## 4. Record your matches if possible

Video is the best way to get accurate stats.

Set up a phone, GoPro, or camera on the halfway line if your club allows it. Afterward, rewatch and track:

- Passes completed/attempted
- First touch quality
- Positioning
- Decision-making
- Defensive recovery runs
- Pressing moments
- Movement off the ball

When reviewing video, use timestamps:

| Time | Event | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 12:30 | Lost ball | Took extra touch under pressure |
| 27:10 | Key pass | Good scan before receiving |
| 61:45 | Missed run | Didn’t track runner |

---

## 5. Use a rating system

Stats don’t tell the full story, so rate key areas from 1–10:

- Fitness
- Passing
- Defending
- Attacking contribution
- Communication
- Positioning
- Decision-making
- Work rate
- Confidence

Example:

| Category | Rating |
|---|---:|
| Fitness | 7 |
| Passing | 8 |
| Positioning | 6 |
| Work rate | 9 |
| Decision-making | 7 |

Over time, this helps you spot patterns.

---

## 6. Track physical stats if you can

If you have a smartwatch, GPS vest, or running app, you can monitor:

- Distance covered
- Sprint distance
- Top speed
- Average speed
- Heart rate
- Calories burned
- Workload over the week

Grassroots players don’t need elite-level tech, but even basic distance and sprint tracking can help with fitness.

Useful options include:
- Smartwatch fitness apps
- Strava
- Garmin / Apple Watch / Fitbit
- Football GPS trackers if you want something more serious

---

## 7. Create monthly summaries

Every month, review your numbers.

Look for trends like:

- Are you playing more minutes?
- Are your pass completion numbers improving?
- Are you creating more chances?
- Are you losing the ball less?
- Are you winning more duels?
- Are you contributing goals/assists?
- Is your fitness improving?

Example monthly summary:

| Month | Games | Goals | Assists | Avg Rating | Main Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| September | 4 | 2 | 1 | 7.1 | Better crossing |
| October | 5 | 3 | 3 | 7.8 | More confident shooting |

---

## 8. Keep it honest and consistent

Your stats only help if they’re realistic.

A few tips:

- Use the same definitions every match
- Don’t exaggerate numbers
- Include mistakes as well as positives
- Track performance, not just goals
- Compare yourself to your past self, not everyone else

---

## Simple starter template

For each match, write this:

**Match:**  
**Date:**  
**Opponent:**  
**Position:**  
**Minutes:**  
**Result:**  

**Stats:**  
- Goals:
- Assists:
- Shots:
- Passes completed/attempted:
- Tackles won:
- Interceptions:
- Fouls:
- Rating /10:

**Reflection:**  
- Best moment:
- Biggest mistake:
- What I learned:
- Focus for next match:

---

If you want the simplest version: use a **Google Sheet**, track **minutes, goals, assists, shots, pass completion, tackles, interceptions, and match rating**, then add **one short note after every game**. That alone will give you a clear picture of your progress over the season.
